content:
Yes—you can start tomato seeds in bunches, and many people do. It works well as long as you separate (or thin) the seedlings early enough.

**Two common ways:**

1) **Sow several seeds per cell/pot (a “clump”)**
- Plant 2–5 seeds in one cell or small pot.
- After they sprout, **thin to the strongest 1 plant** *or* **separate them** once they have their first set of **true leaves** (the leaves after the initial smooth “seed leaves”).
- If separating, gently tease roots apart (best when small) and pot each up.

2) **Sow densely in a tray (community flat)**
- Sprinkle seeds in rows or a patch.
- When seedlings have **true leaves**, prick them out and pot up individually.

**Tips to make bunch-starting succeed**
- Don’t wait too long to separate—tomato roots tangle quickly.
- Use a light seed-starting mix and keep evenly moist (not soggy).
- Provide strong light so they don’t get leggy.
- When potting up, you can **bury tomato stems deeper** (they root along the stem).

If you tell me whether you’re using cells, small pots, or a tray—and how many plants you ultimately want—I can suggest the easiest method and spacing.
